scenes.title: G major
scenes.subtitle: A big, six-string chord.
lines: This lesson teaches the G major chord — a big, six-string shape.
We'll play it with your first three fingers, and move to it from C major in the next lesson.

scenes.heading: G major (G)
lines: Place finger 2 on string 6 at fret 3, finger 1 on string 5 at fret 2, and finger 3 on string 1 at fret 3.
Keep fingers arched so strings 4, 3 and 2 ring open.
Take your time — smooth changes come with practice.
The G major chord is a bright, open sound that's perfect for beginners — here's how to place your fingers.
Here's how it sounds: strummed, then string by string.
scenes.tip: Stay on the tips of fingers 1 and 2 so strings 4, 3 and 2 ring open; that's where G gets its bright sound.

lines: Let's practice changing between G major and D major.
Move your fingers smoothly from one shape to the next, one chord at a time.
Place your fingers as we practiced, and play G major while the app listens and guides you.
